baseline: C mix: gear -9 dB, rolling +2 dB in CSV; steady whine and residual reductions baked into WAVs
mechanical_rule: Play these four layers continuously in every motion mode, at their CSV gains, without demand scaling. Preserve loop read heads through mode changes. Duplicate power/brake mechanical assets have been removed.
scope: Requires explicit support in the player; loading only curves.csv with coast-only gating will not reproduce the accepted previews.
not_yet_tested: C mix has been approved in the 14 m/s demos. Other speeds and in-game C playback still need listening checks.
settings_format: proposed custom player metadata, not an existing game standard
status: C balance accepted at 14 m/s; extension to other steady speeds awaits listening
smoothstep: s(u)=3*u*u-2*u*u*u, u clamped to [0,1]; interpolate from current envelope gain to its new target
power_layer_selection: Every layer with CSV mode power, including upper_ layers
steady_settings_format: Addon keys to merge into existing player settings; plain-language rules are normative for this proposed extension.
steady_blend_rule: Within each existing power/brake family, smoothstep from the current steady fraction to the new target over 1.5 seconds, both entering and leaving steady load. Keep independent power and brake steady fractions. Do not use an equal-power crossfade or restart from an endpoint after an interruption.
steady_hold_rule: Require the same existing load classification, valid family availability, speed in range, and the steady entry tests continuously for 1.25 seconds before targeting steady fraction 1. Coasting does not prequalify a later load. Reset the qualifying timer on failure or a family change.
steady_enter_rule: Use speed magnitude and actual delta-speed/delta-time, not gravity-compensated effort. For entry, absolute acceleration must be at most 0.08 m/s² and the maximum minus minimum speed over the preceding 1.25 seconds must be at most 0.18 m/s. Existing grade-aware classification independently decides power versus brake.
steady_exit_rule: Player revision after the first in-game ride: Create's curve speed cap lifts for a few ticks at track joins and steps the speed about 0.25 m/s above the held speed and back, which ended steady load under the original 0.15 m/s² for 0.15 s rule. Steady now targets fraction 0 only when the speed is at least 0.5 m/s from the held speed and the net acceleration over the last 0.4 seconds is at least 0.15 m/s². A drift past 0.5 m/s at a lower acceleration moves the held speed instead. The held speed is the middle of the qualifying speed span. A family change, invalid family availability, or speed outside the eligibility range targets 0 immediately. Existing electrical availability and mode gain gates still apply immediately according to their existing rules.
steady_speed_rule: Eligibility includes 5 and 40 m/s. The extra zero-volume rows below 5 m/s provide a fade guard during exit; they do not enable steady load below 5 m/s.
steady_gain_rule: Let P and B be existing smoothed demand/mode/availability gains in [0,1], and SP and SB the separate steady fractions. Original power gain is P*(1-SP); power_steady is P*SP. Original brake gain is B*(1-SB); brake_steady is B*SB. Multiply each by its own speed-table volume. Do not add a second copy at full gain or lower the family gain just because measured acceleration is zero.
steady_cruising_duck_rule: Keep cruising gain = its CSV volume * (1 - 0.85 * max(P,B)), using total family gains before steady partitioning. Do not use only the original sweep gains, or sum the steady gains a second time.
steady_mechanical_rule: Continuous mechanical layers use updated CSV gains. Do not partition, restart or demand-scale them. Cruising also retains its read head.
steady_loop_rule: Play every nonzero-volume row in the active steady family. The a/b/c files are simultaneous components, not alternatives. Keep their independent read heads continuous across entry, speed changes, and exit. Retain phase while inaudible, for example by advancing a virtual read head. Never align or restart all components at a loop boundary.
steady_existing_mode_timing_rule: Keep existing 0.25-second mode blend and 1-second slope-load ramp, with the additional 1.5-second steady blend. Curves are already combined; do not append older addon rows.
steady_contact_rule: Honor the player's existing availability gate for each family. Loss of contact disables power as it already does. Use the existing electrical-braking availability rule for brake_steady; do not invent a new brake availability rule from this addon. Driver direction input alone is not a steady-load requirement.
steady_status: Updated C balance; 14 m/s approved, other anchors extrapolated using the same spectral treatment
mix_rule: Use files and CSV exactly once. Do not apply additional C EQ or gear/rolling gain changes: they are already baked into assets or CSV.
player_keys_note: Keys from here on are not in the wmata-alstom-C-v4 delivery. They carry the player's existing cruising duck, mode timing and slope ramp, which INTEGRATION.md says to keep; steady_exit_hold_seconds, steady_exit_speed_deviation_mps and steady_exit_rule above also keep the player's tested exit revision in place of the delivery's 0.15 s rule.
ducked_rule: wmata-cruising-addon: play continuously while moving, not gated by coast mode, at CSV volume x (1 - duck_depth x max(power_gain, brake_gain)) using the smoothed envelope gains.
mode_change_rule: wmata-cruising-addon: above departure_speed_mps a new mode must persist for mode_persistence_seconds, then every mode envelope blends from its current gain over mode_blend_seconds. Below it (departing from rest) the accepted power_on, power_off and brake_on timings apply unchanged.
slope_rule: Create doesn't slow trains on hills, so gravity along the slope counts as traction demand: holding speed on a climb powers, on a descent brakes. Power brought in by a climb (not by speeding up) swells in over slope_power_blend_seconds. While a driver holds a direction, slowing imposed by Create's speed limits counts as neither braking nor powering.
mode_end_rule: While moving, the end of power or brake demand must hold for mode_end_persistence_seconds before cruising takes over, so demand handing from a slope to speeding up (at a crest, or as Create lifts a speed cap) doesn't dip to cruise.
mode_power_rule: While moving, powering must hold for mode_power_persistence_seconds before it takes effect, so the moment Create lifts a speed cap on a short straight between track pieces doesn't swell the power layers in and out.
